1

Purpose

This procedure enables users to quickly create a new dashboard and populate it with a bar chart widget displaying task status. Sharing the dashboard link allows for easy collaboration and visibility of key task information across teams, facilitating improved workflow management and project tracking.

The process covers the following tasks:

  • Create a New dashboard
  • Add a Bar Chart Widget
  • Edit Widget Title and Share
In short

The session demonstrated how to create and share a new dashboard. The process began by navigating to the dashboards menu and selecting the option to create a new one, which was named "Weekly Overview" using a blank template. A bar chart widget was then added to the dashboard, populated with data representing tasks by status. The widget’s title was edited to read "tasks this week" for clarity. Finally, the dashboard was shared by enabling access via a link, which was then copied for distribution.

Step by step

Follow the parts in order. Each numbered action matches a marker on the screenshot below it. Click a screenshot to enlarge it.

Part A

Create a New dashboard

00:00
A1

Click 'Dashboards' in the navigation menu.

A2

Click 'New dashboard'.

A3

Enter 'Weekly Overview' as the dashboard name.

A4

Select the 'Blank' template.

A5

Click 'Create'.

Result

A new dashboard named 'Weekly Overview' is created with a blank template.

Tip

Remember to give your dashboard a descriptive name for easy identification.

Watch it · click to enlarge
Part B

Add a Bar Chart Widget

00:21
B1

Click 'Add widget' on the Weekly Overview dashboard.

B2

Select 'Bar chart' from the 'Add widget' dialog.

B3

Choose 'Tasks by status' from the 'Choose data' dropdown.

B4

Click 'Add' to create the bar chart widget (see Figure 5).

B5

Click 'edit' on the 'Tasks by status' widget.

B6

Type 'Tasks this week' into the 'Edit title' field.

Result

A bar chart widget displaying 'Tasks by status' is added to the dashboard, and its title is updated to 'Tasks this week'.

Tip

The 'Add widget' dialog provides options for different chart types.

Watch it · click to enlarge
Part C

Edit Widget Title and Share

00:39
C1

Click Edit

C2

Click Save

C3

Click Share

C4

Enable 'Anyone with the link can view'

C5

Click the link to copy it

Result

The widget title is updated to 'Tasks this week', dashboard sharing is enabled for anyone with the link, and the link has been copied to the clipboard.

Tip

The 'Share dashboard' panel allows sharing with 'Anyone with the link'.

Questions and answers

Questions raised in the recording, plus ones a new reader may have.

Why does choosing a "blank template" when creating a new dashboard matter, and are there other template options available?+

Choosing a "blank template" when creating a new dashboard means you're starting from scratch without any pre-existing visualizations or layout. The transcript excerpts indicate that this is an option available when creating a new dashboard, but do not mention any other template options. This allows for complete customization of the dashboard's design and content.

What does "tasks by status" refer to when selecting data for the bar chart widget?+

"Tasks by status" refers to the data selection method used when creating the bar chart widget; it's the initial choice made when adding data to the dashboard. This selection allows the bar chart to display tasks categorized by their current status. After selecting this data, the user then clicks "add" to proceed with creating the chart.

If I want to restrict sharing to only specific team members instead of "anyone with the link," what alternative sharing options exist?+

To restrict sharing, you can disable the "anyone with the link" option and instead share with specific team members. This allows you to control who has access, rather than making the information publicly available via a link. The process involves clicking "Share" and then adjusting the sharing settings to limit access to designated team members.

When should I consider using a different type of widget besides a bar chart for my dashboard?+

The transcript does not provide any guidance on when to use a different type of widget; it only demonstrates how to create a dashboard using a bar chart. The procedure involves adding a widget, selecting a bar chart, and then editing the chart's title to "tasks this week." the app, the excerpt does not address alternative widget choices.

What happens if I accidentally choose the wrong data source when adding a widget, and how can I correct it?+

If you select the incorrect data source when adding a widget, you can correct it by choosing "tasks by status" and then clicking "add." This action allows you to adjust the data being used for the widget.

Is there a limit to the number of widgets I can add to a single dashboard?+

The provided transcript excerpts do not mention any limits on the number of widgets that can be added to a dashboard. The instructions simply state to click "Add widget" to populate the dashboard with data, such as "tasks by status."
